story.iWant: manage personas via YAML + CLI commands
story.soThat: I can tune the Council of Ricks without editing code
story.tasks: - Task 1: Define persona schema and YAML structure * Create src/jarvis/agents/config/personas.yaml with schema * Add pydantic schema PersonaConfig in src/jarvis/agents/personas.py * Validate weight totals sum to 100% across enabled personas * Add JSON schema documentation - Task 2: Implement persona storage in PostgreSQL * Design personas table schema (already exists in models.py - AgentPersona) * Create Alembic migration (table already created in initial migration 0f3513bed9f3) * Implement PersonaModel in src/jarvis/database/models.py (already exists!) * Add CRUD operations for persona management - Task 3: Build CLI commands for persona management * Create src/jarvis/cli/commands/personas.py with Typer app * Implement jarvis personas list/add/update/enable/disable * Add parameter validation and error handling - Task 4: Implement hot-reload for persona changes * Add persona registry watcher in src/jarvis/agents/orchestrator.py * Implement hot-reload mechanism using importlib.reload() * Sync YAML changes to PostgreSQL on file modification - Task 5: Tests (all ACs) * Unit tests for PersonaConfig pydantic schema validation * Unit tests for weight totals validation (must sum to 100%) * Unit tests for CLI command parsing and validation * Integration test: personas YAML → PostgreSQL sync * Integration test: hot-reload on personas.yaml modification

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Given personas.yaml defines agents, When the user runs "jarvis personas list/add/update", Then personas sync to PostgreSQL and the CLI validates weight totals, And changes hot-reload without restart.

artifact.reason: AgentPersona model ALREADY EXISTS with id, name, system_prompt, weight (Numeric 3,2), is_active, created_at fields. Table created in initial migration. DO NOT recreate - reuse this model.

Demonstrates pydantic @dataclass pattern with Settings.from_dict() for YAML loading. Shows validation, type coercion, and clamping patterns (lines 93-98 expansion_count clamping). Extend with PersonaConfig dataclass.

Typer CLI command pattern: app = typer.Typer(), @app.command() decorator, parameter validation (lines 67-89), config precedence (CLI overrides YAML), error messages with typer.echo() and typer.Exit(code=1).
Alembic migration example. Shows agent_personas table ALREADY CREATED (lines 25-34) with correct schema. DO NOT create duplicate migration - table exists. Use for reference or extend if needed.
Unit test pattern for CLI commands: use typer.testing.CliRunner, pytest.fixture for mocks, unittest.mock.patch for dependencies, assert result.exit_code == 0 for success.

story-context.constraints: - CRITICAL: AgentPersona model and agent_personas table ALREADY EXIST. DO NOT recreate. tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest 8.3+ with coverage reporting (--cov=jarvis --cov-report=term-missing). Unit tests: Use pytest fixtures for mocks, unittest.mock.patch for dependencies, MagicMock for test doubles. CLI tests: Use typer.testing.CliRunner, assert result.exit_code for success/failure. Integration tests: Mark with @pytest.mark.integration, require Docker services (PostgreSQL). Coverage target: High coverage on new code (aim for 90%+ on persona module). Test structure: Arrange-Act-Assert pattern, descriptive test names (test_weight_validation_sum_not_100_raises_error). Assertions: Use specific assertions (assert result.exit_code == 0, assert "error message" in result.stdout).
tests.locations: - tests/unit/agents/ - Unit tests for persona schema and validation - tests/unit/cli/ - CLI command tests with CliRunner - tests/integration/agents/ - Hot-reload integration tests - tests/integration/cli/ - End-to-end CLI integration tests
